problem: Internal architecture of 'lifecycle_gate' (type: Subservice — Internal control-plane subservice running as part of the region_coordinator quorum across regions. Holds no canonical state outside the consensus substrate; mutations are proposed via quorum_core, reads come from state_log.). Node: Single scheduler-of-record for cross-component lifecycle operations against shared targets, scheduling and gating lifecycle events globally via CAS proposals through quorum_core into control_lane: cert/origin rotations (region-staggered), chain pool rotations (one pool, one region, one wave at a time, admitted only while canonical-tip quorum size remains above safe threshold), region-drain events, schema-version capability bumps (two-phase: deploy then activate), operational pauses (VM live migration etc), residency-policy activation windows, credential_roster rotation activation windows, anchor rotation, decommission-handoff-transfer (decommissioning a successor buffer that owns drain-ack-handoff records — admitted only when every pending-flush handoff record on the buffer is either resolved or transferred-to-another-successor), bulk-offboarding wave admission, operator-override classification (gateway_health_surface single-region cross-witness-pending promotion under M-of-N elevated-tier-A), and operator-override probationary-fork admissions. Cert rotations on the inter-region channel admitted only when remaining validity exceeds documented overlap budget; if breached, lifecycle_gate raises emergency-cert-recovery in control_lane and stops admitting any non-cert-rotation lifecycle events; recovery delegated to cert_bootstrap. CAS proposals attach the latest read of (per-(chain, fork) quorum-size set, rotation-in-progress set, tip-stale set, schema-capability config, drain-in-progress set, pause-in-progress set, current roster_version, compromise-revoked credential set, lease-issuance state, residency policy_version, prepared-ack set, residency-2PC-in-flight lock set per tenant, lease-quiescent flag set per tenant, anchor-healthy count, drain-ack-handoff records and their resolution state, lease_issuer routine-budget headroom, lease_issuer dedicated lease-revoke sub-budget headroom, lease_issuer lease-reissue sub-budget headroom, named-writer queue depths, in-flight residency 2PC PREPARE count and watermark) as the precondition; commit re-validates atomically. Per-tenant residency-2PC-in-flight lock: lifecycle_gate maintains the lock in control_lane; PREPARE commit acquires; COMMIT/ABORT/PREPARED-ORPHAN releases; competing PREPARE for the same tenant T is CAS-rejected with reason 'residency-2PC-already-in-flight'. credential_roster rotation-activate is admitted only after all in-flight residency 2PCs have reached terminal state under prior roster, OR rotation-activate explicitly carries a residency-2PC-cancel-and-abort directive (elevated-tier-A) issuing idempotent abort-V+1 entries for every in-flight residency 2PC atomically before activation. Rotation-activate records an explicit rotation-activation-HLC in control_lane (s4-7): records signed strictly before this HLC verify under V_old and records signed strictly after verify under V_new; credential_roster MUST retain V_old as verifiable for at least max(residency-2PC-in-flight-lock max-window, drain-ack-handoff record SLA max-window) past activation. At most one region-drain plus one pool-rotation in flight globally. Tags rotation-in-progress, drain-in-progress, pause-in-progress in control_lane so chain_router (parent) suppresses quarantines and hlc_service applies pause-aware bounds. Operator-override admission delegates credential validation to credential_roster's published roster: every override CAS proposal must carry M-of-N signatures drawn from active roster_version named in CAS precondition; lifecycle_gate validates each signature against credential_roster's published state in control_lane and rejects fast on insufficient signers, signers in compromise-revoked set, or validity-window mismatch; admission record persists signing operator identities into control_lane. In-flight override proposals invalidated on credential transitions into compromise-revoked between admission and commit (CAS rejection with credential-revoked-mid-flight reason). Drain-fence-broadcast originator (PHASE A): on observing erasure-tombstone in tombstone_lane for tenant T, computes fence_HLC f_T and broadcasts drain-fence-broadcast(T, f_T, signing roster_version) to every named writer (region_coordinator subservices internally + parent-scope chain_router, gateway, fanout, address_index, usage_meter). Broadcasts carry signing roster_version as part of the broadcast itself; consumers verify against the broadcast's NAMED roster_version. On compromise-revocation events from credential_roster carrying retroactive-as-of-HLC, lifecycle_gate re-signs and re-broadcasts in-flight broadcasts whose emit-HLC >= retroactive-as-of-HLC: re-emission does NOT reset per-tenant ack windows for tenants whose phase markers had already reached an ack-completed phase under the original signing — re-emission carries a per-tenant signature-only-update annotation that updates the broadcast's signing roster_version in offboarding_orchestrator's phase marker without resetting the ack window; only tenants not yet ack-completed receive a fresh ack window. Re-emission has its own dedicated bandwidth budget within lifecycle_gate's broadcast pipeline, separate from new-wave admission, sized as a fraction of total broadcast pipeline capacity to bound impact on new-wave admission. Broadcast pipeline shed-and-defer (s4-1): when in-flight residency 2PC PREPAREs exceed a configured watermark, lifecycle_gate sheds-and-defers non-critical PHASE A audit-key destruction entries by writing explicit deferral records to control_lane with cause and HLC; deferred entries are re-emitted automatically when the watermark clears, with no silent stall. Bounded-batching for bulk-offboarding: lifecycle_gate admits bulk-offboarding requests into bounded waves with documented max-tenants-per-wave and inter-wave spacing; wave admission CAS proposal includes lease_issuer's dedicated lease-revoke sub-budget headroom (NOT total lease_lane capacity — bulk-wave is budgeted strictly against the lease-revoke-priority sub-stream per s4-2) AND every named-writer's bounded queue depth AND the residency-2PC-in-flight lock set as preconditions; admission rejected with reason 'lease-issuer-budget-insufficient' or 'writer-queue-full' or 'residency-2PC-conflict' when precondition fails; bulk-admission backs off with exponential-with-jitter; per-writer bounded ack queues with explicit back-pressure stall further wave admission for that writer rather than dropping broadcasts or expiring per-tenant HLC windows; per-tenant HLC-bounded ack windows start from per-tenant ack-broadcast-emit-HLC; bulk-offboarding admission is itself a CAS-committed operator-credentialed proposal and audited via compliance_audit_owner. Bulk-wave start and end markers (s4-6): lifecycle_gate publishes bulk-wave-start and bulk-wave-end markers on control_lane carrying (offboarding_id, wave_id, expected-region-set, expected-degradation-envelope) so health_lane consumers can correlate classification entries with the wave via wave_id. Compromise-revocation lease-reissue back-pressure (s4-5): lifecycle_gate surfaces an explicit back-pressure signal (recorded in control_lane and paged on-call) when the lease-reissue sub-stream budget saturates beyond a configurable horizon following a compromise-revocation broadcast; the signal carries the elapsed reissue lag and the count of pending reissues. Teardown-overlap sequencing: a node-teardown is not admitted while any in-flight per-tenant drain-fence on that node is unacked; nodes that cannot flush within their teardown window write a durable drain-ack-handoff record to lease_lane (or tombstone_lane, schema-tagged) naming a successor instance or persistent buffer; ack-by-handoff is treated as ack only after the handoff record resolves to handoff-flushed terminal state OR is resolved-with-loss-attestation under operator M-of-N. Decommissioning a successor buffer is itself a lifecycle event admitted by lifecycle_gate that requires all pending-flush handoff records the buffer owns to be either resolved or transferred-to-another-successor (recursive handoff re-applying the same SLA contract); a buffer cannot be decommissioned while any unresolved handoff is still owned by it. Audit-key destruction PHASE B: lifecycle_gate's PHASE B CAS proposal includes lease-quiescent(T) precondition (no active or prepared lease for T, no in-flight handoff-fence for T) AND every drain-ack-handoff record for T resolved-or-no-residual-writes-expected. t_destroy = max(observed_ack_hlc, f_T + skew_bound) + write-delivery-grace, computed using observed_ack_hlc only when EVERY contributing drain-ack was emitted under healthy hlc_service (drain-ack hlc_service-status annotation = healthy); otherwise t_destroy is computed from the worst-case drain-ack-pause-deferred completion HLC + skew_bound + write-delivery-grace and PHASE B does not commit until any pause-window has ended and a healthy-mode drain-ack has landed for affected writers. PHASE B CAS-commits an audit-key DESTROYED entry to lease_lane at HLC >= t_destroy; the DESTROYED entry triggers compliance_audit_owner's tenant-key-scoped late-write rejection cutoff at compliance_audit (parent). PHASE B does not commit while any drain-ack for T is outstanding from a named writer, including drain-ack-handoff records still in pending-flush state (unless explicitly resolved-with-loss-attestation under operator M-of-N). All lifecycle events, override admissions, drain-fence broadcasts, drain-acks, drain-ack-handoff resolutions, decommission-handoff-transfers, audit-key DESTROYED writes, broadcast-pipeline deferral records, bulk-wave start/end markers, lease-reissue back-pressure signals, and rotation-activation-HLC entries are typed-audited via compliance_audit_owner's schema registry. (Realizes inherited r-s5-drain-fence-protocol, r-s5-drain-fence-bounded-batching, r-s5-drain-fence-teardown-overlap, r-s5-broadcast-self-contained-credential, r-s5-audit-key-destruction-fence; addresses zoom stressors s6-lease-handoff-vs-destroy, s6-policy-roster-coactivation, s3-handoff-record-orphan, s3-cross-witness-partition, s3-anchor-quorum-silent-failure, s3-bulk-lease-revoke-budget, s3-skew-degraded-ack-hlc, s3-resign-rebroadcast-storm; addresses s4-1 via broadcast-pipeline shed-and-defer, s4-2 via bulk-wave admission against lease-revoke-priority sub-stream budget, s4-5 via lease-reissue back-pressure surfacing, s4-6 via bulk-wave start/end markers, s4-7 via rotation-activation-HLC boundary recording.). Connections: lifecycle_gate --calls-> tip_quorum; lifecycle_gate --calls-> quorum_core; lifecycle_gate --calls-> hlc_service; lifecycle_gate --reads_from-> control_lane; lifecycle_gate --reads_from-> tip_lane; lifecycle_gate --calls-> compliance_audit_owner. Parent requirements: IR-cert-rotation-staggered: Cert and origin-endpoint rotations are region-staggered: at most one region transitions a given cert-bearing surface inside a maintenance window. Simultaneous expiry across regions is prevented by construction.; IR-origin-rotation: Origin endpoints (gateway-accepted IP/hostname pairs) rotate on a documented cadence under the same region-staggered gate as cert rotation.; IR-rotation-coordinator-gate: Chain pool rotations are gated globally to one pool, one region, one wave at a time, and are admitted only while the canonical-tip quorum size remains above its safe threshold throughout.; IR-rotation-aware-skew: Rotation events surface a 'rotation in progress' tag in state_log so chain_router's schema-skew and tip-divergence quarantines suppress quarantines triggered solely by the documented rotation window.; SR1-rotation-cas-admission: Pool-rotation admission is committed via quorum_core as a CAS proposal that includes its own preconditions (per-(chain, fork) quorum-size set, rotation-in-progress set, tip-stale set); the proposal commits only if those preconditions still hold at commit time.; SR1-rotation-precondition-revalidate: On rejection, lifecycle_gate re-reads the latest applied state and may re-propose with refreshed preconditions; lifecycle_gate never relies on a precondition snapshot older than its current proposal.; SR1-schema-rollout-gated: Replica code rollouts that introduce a new schema_version are region-staggered under lifecycle_gate; the schema-capability config entry is committed only after every replica has been upgraded — a two-phase upgrade (deploy, then activate).; SR1-region-drain-event: Region-drain is a first-class lifecycle event in state_log distinct from pool rotation; lifecycle_gate schedules and admits it through the same CAS proposal mechanism.; SR1-drain-aware-threshold: lifecycle_gate's quorum-size safety threshold is evaluated against the post-drain configuration: rotations are not blocked merely because a drain is in flight, but rotations whose admission would drop the post-drain quorum below safe are rejected.; SR1-mutual-scheduling: At most one region-drain plus one pool-rotation are in flight globally; mutual scheduling is enforced by lifecycle_gate's admission rules so drains and rotations cannot starve each other indefinitely.; SR2-probationary-override: An operator-override admission path exists for probationary forks: lifecycle_gate accepts a CAS proposal that admits a probationary (chain, fork_id) over the threshold shortfall, gated on the absent-region-set being explainable by current drain-in-progress or rotation-in-progress entries in control_lane. The override commits to tip_lane with operator attribution and is visible in tip_quorum's reorg notifications.; SR2-cert-overlap-window: Inter-region channel cert rotation runs with an overlap window: lifecycle_gate admits a cert rotation only when remaining validity on the active cert exceeds a documented overlap budget. During the overlap, both old and new cert are trusted on the inter-region channel so consensus on the rotation itself rides the old cert while the new cert is distributed via control_lane; trust handover to the new cert is atomic at the HLC effective-from stamp recorded with the rotation entry.; SR2-cert-emergency-recovery: If the overlap window is breached (no successful rotation committed before the active cert nears expiry), lifecycle_gate raises an emergency-cert-recovery event in control_lane and stops admitting any non-cert-rotation lifecycle events. Recovery from total cert expiry is delegated to a parent-scope out-of-band bootstrap surface — region_coordinator alone cannot recover consensus over a channel whose only authenticator has expired.; SR2-pause-event-class: Documented operational pauses (VM live migration and any successor pause classes) are first-class lifecycle events scheduled and admitted by lifecycle_gate via CAS into control_lane, with a recorded pause-window and the affected region(s).; r-zoom-rc-broadcast-self-contained: lifecycle_gate-signed broadcasts (drain-fence in particular) carry the signing roster_version as part of the broadcast itself; consumers verify signatures against the broadcast's NAMED roster_version, not a cached version. Signed broadcasts remain verifiable for the duration of their HLC-bounded ack window even after a scheduled roster rotation activates a strictly newer version.; r-zoom-rc-drain-fence: lifecycle_gate originates drain-fence broadcasts on observing erasure-tombstone for tenant T; broadcast carries fence-HLC f_T and signing roster_version; every named writer flushes in-flight audit writes for T to compliance_audit then acks drain to tenant_store within the HLC-bounded ack window; offboarding_orchestrator tracks per-(T, writer) ack state via durable phase markers.; r-zoom-rc-bounded-batching: lifecycle_gate admits bulk-offboarding waves with documented max-tenants-per-wave and inter-wave spacing; per-writer bounded ack queues with explicit back-pressure stall further wave admission rather than dropping broadcasts or expiring HLC windows; per-tenant HLC-bounded ack windows start from per-tenant ack-broadcast-emit-HLC, not from the bulk operator action HLC.; r-zoom-rc-teardown-overlap: lifecycle_gate's teardown-overlap interlock: node-teardown is not admitted while any in-flight per-tenant drain-fence on that node is unacked. Nodes that cannot flush within their teardown window write a durable drain-ack-handoff record naming a successor instance or persistent buffer; ack-by-handoff is treated as ack for the certificate of deletion. No silent drop and no unbounded wait.; r-zoom-rc-residency-2pc-lock: lifecycle_gate maintains a per-tenant residency-2PC-in-flight lock in control_lane: PREPARE commit acquires; COMMIT/ABORT/PREPARED-ORPHAN release; competing PREPARE for same tenant T is CAS-rejected with reason 'residency-2PC-already-in-flight'. The lock is HLC-bounded (matches prepared-window). PREPARED-ORPHAN is a terminal state per (tenant_key, V+1) tuple — fresh attempt_id cannot escape PREPARED-ORPHAN; recovery requires operator M-of-N elevated AND tenant_store clean-rollback-complete.; r-zoom-rc-decommission-handoff-transfer: Decommissioning a successor buffer is a lifecycle event admitted by lifecycle_gate that requires all pending-flush handoff records the buffer owns to be either resolved or transferred-to-another-successor (recursive handoff re-applying the same SLA contract); a buffer cannot be decommissioned while any unresolved handoff is still owned by it.; r-zoom-rc-health-operator-override: lifecycle_gate may issue an operator-override classification (under M-of-N from credential_roster's published roster) that promotes a single-region classification past the cross-witness window with operator attribution recorded into health_lane and audited via compliance_audit_owner.; r-zoom-rc-budget-coupled-admission: lifecycle_gate's bulk-offboarding wave admission CAS proposal includes lease_issuer's CAS budget headroom and every named-writer's bounded queue depth as preconditions; admission is rejected with 'lease-issuer-budget-insufficient' or 'writer-queue-full' when the precondition fails; bulk-admission backs off with exponential-with-jitter. lease_issuer publishes its current CAS budget headroom to control_lane.; r-zoom-rc-phase-b-healthy-only: lifecycle_gate's PHASE B t_destroy computation uses observed_ack_hlc only when every contributing drain-ack was emitted under healthy hlc_service; otherwise t_destroy is computed from the worst-case drain-ack-pause-deferred completion HLC + skew_bound + write-delivery-grace. PHASE B does not commit until any pause-window has ended and a healthy-mode drain-ack has landed for affected writers.; r-zoom-rc-resign-no-window-reset: Re-sign-and-rebroadcast does not reset per-tenant ack windows for tenants whose broadcast had already reached an ack-completed phase (FLUSH-COMPLETE, ACK-EMITTED, ATTESTATION-WRITTEN, TERMINAL); lifecycle_gate's re-emission carries a per-tenant signature-only-update annotation updating the broadcast's signing roster_version in offboarding_orchestrator's phase marker without resetting the window. Only tenants not yet ack-completed receive a fresh ack window.; r-zoom-rc-resign-dedicated-budget: Re-emission has its own dedicated bandwidth budget within lifecycle_gate's broadcast pipeline, separate from new-wave admission, sized as a fraction of total broadcast pipeline capacity to bound impact on new-wave admission.; r-s4-1-broadcast-shed-defer: lifecycle_gate broadcast pipeline MUST shed-and-defer non-critical PHASE A audit-key destruction entries when in-flight residency 2PC PREPAREs exceed a configured watermark; deferred entries are written as explicit deferral records in control_lane with cause and HLC, and re-emitted when the watermark clears, with no silent stall.; r-s4-2-bulk-wave-revoke-budget: lifecycle_gate bulk-wave admission MUST budget bulk-offboarding throughput against lease-revoke-priority sub-stream capacity (not total lease_lane capacity); back-pressure on bulk-wave is signaled when the revoke sub-stream nears its budget independent of lease-prepared occupancy.; r-s4-5-reissue-backpressure: lifecycle_gate MUST surface an explicit back-pressure signal (recorded in control_lane and paged on-call) when the lease-reissue sub-stream budget saturates beyond a configurable horizon following a compromise-revocation broadcast; the signal carries the elapsed reissue lag and the count of pending reissues.; r-s4-6-bulk-wave-markers: lifecycle_gate MUST publish bulk-wave start and end markers on control_lane carrying (offboarding_id, wave_id, expected-region-set, expected-degradation-envelope); health_lane consumers MUST correlate classification entries with these markers via wave_id.; r-s4-7-rotation-activation-hlc-boundary: lifecycle_gate's rotation-activate MUST record an activation HLC; records signed strictly before the activation HLC verify under V_old and records signed strictly after verify under V_new. credential_roster MUST retain V_old as verifiable for at least max(residency-2PC-in-flight-lock max-window, handoff-record SLA max-window) past activation.

versions.note: v0 — Naive lifecycle_gate sub-zoom: 6 subsystems (broadcast_pipeline, bulk_admitter, residency_lock, audit_destruct_sequencer, credential_validator, teardown_interlock) wired through 5 lane handles and 7 external dep handles; 16 inherited reqs all satisfied. CRITICAL K̄=2.11 P̄=0.65 modularity=0.95.

v1 — Direction 17 Session 1 against v0. Ran 13 stressors across re-emission/burst, residency-2PC FIFO/override re-aim, PHASE A→B health regression, retroactive credential revocation mid-validation, handoff cycle/orphan detection, budget-staleness under degraded HLC, drain-ack signing under retroactive revocation, override-flood tiering (Tier-A/B/C), shed-and-defer collision with re-sign, wave-end premature finalization, lock teardown overlap with decommission, audit-channel saturation (inline vs deferred), and cold-start partial-collection recovery. All 29 derived reqs satisfied via redefining all 6 subsystem nodes plus ext_hlc_service and ext_lease_issuer handles. 6 bubbles up to parent. CRITICAL K̄=2.11 P̄=0.65 modularity=0.95.

stressors.description: Long roster-rotation window: credential_roster issues compromise-revocation with retroactive-as-of-HLC covering thousands of in-flight broadcasts (bulk-offboarding wave already in progress). broadcast_pipeline's dedicated re-emission budget — sized as a fraction of total capacity — is sized for steady-state revocation, not for a worst-case mass re-sign event coinciding with peak new-wave throughput. Re-emission queues backlog past the per-tenant ack window for not-yet-ack-completed tenants while signature-only-update annotations for ack-completed tenants compete for the same sub-stream.
stressors.attractor: Re-emission backlog grows unbounded during the rotation window; ack windows expire for not-yet-ack-completed tenants under V_old; tenant_store's drain-ack timeout fires; offboarding_orchestrator phase markers regress; PHASE B refuses to advance and audit-key destruction stalls indefinitely.
stressors.solution: Decompose the re-emission sub-stream into two priority classes: (a) signature-only-update annotations (cheap, no envelope payload re-transmit) get a strict-priority lane; (b) full-envelope re-sign-and-rebroadcast for not-yet-ack-completed tenants gets the budgeted lane. Surface a re-emission-budget-saturation back-pressure signal symmetric to the lease-reissue back-pressure on lane_control with elapsed lag and pending-not-yet-ack-completed-count, paged on-call. credential_roster compromise-revocation broadcasts MUST attach an estimated-affected-broadcast-count so broadcast_pipeline can pre-compute re-emission burst budget; lifecycle_gate raises a re-emission-burst-pending event into control_lane and pauses new bulk-wave admission until burst is drained.

stressors.description: Operator issues an M-of-N elevated 'residency-2PC-cancel-and-abort' directive (s4-cluster-double-fence path) for tenant T mid-PREPARE, intending to re-aim the policy version. credential_validator validates and admits the abort directive, but the residency_lock release on (T, V+1) ABORT is observed AFTER a competing fresh PREPARE for (T, V+2) is already proposed; the V+2 PREPARE CAS-rejects on a stale precondition snapshot; bulk_admitter waiting on residency-2PC-in-flight precondition for tenant T enters an infinite-retry loop because two adjacent V+1/V+2 versions occupy the lock back-to-back faster than its exponential-with-jitter backoff converges.
stressors.attractor: residency_lock thrashes between adjacent (tenant_key, V) tuples; bulk_admitter's bulk-offboarding waves for tenants sharing residency-locks with override-driven 2PCs starve indefinitely; on-call has no visibility into the override-vs-bulk priority inversion.
stressors.solution: residency_lock acquires MUST be admitted FIFO via a per-tenant-T queue depth published into lane_control; an operator-elevated abort directive carries an explicit 'next-attempt-version-hint' field and the next acquire on (T, V+next) is admitted only after the abort's release+drain-grace HLC has elapsed AND any queued bulk_admitter wave for tenants in the cohort has been given one admission attempt at the cleared lock state. credential_validator records the override's intent-to-re-aim attribution into the lock-state entry so admission ordering can deterministically prioritize fresh PREPAREs vs bulk-wave admissions; lock-fairness signal (lock-acquire-starvation) surfaced on lane_control + paged when a tenant's bulk_admitter retry-count exceeds threshold under override-driven thrash.

stressors.description: audit_destruct_sequencer issued fence_HLC f_T at HLC-mode=healthy and the first wave of drain-acks all carried hlc_service-status=healthy; the t_destroy precondition appears satisfiable by observed_ack_hlc. Just before PHASE B CAS-commits, hlc_service transitions one region to skew-degraded mode; lifecycle_gate's PHASE B CAS proposal observes a mixed health envelope at commit. Current rule says 'every contributing drain-ack was emitted under healthy hlc_service' — but it does NOT say what happens if a region that already acked HEALTHY now degrades; nor does it say whether further drain-acks ALSO must be healthy or whether the snapshot at issuance is enough. Race: a drain-ack pending for one writer arrives skew-degraded after sequencer chose observed_ack_hlc path — t_destroy is computed under healthy assumption but commits with a skew-degraded contributing ack.
stressors.attractor: Audit-key destroyed earlier than the worst-case-pause-deferred path would have permitted; in-flight writes from the now-skew-degraded region for tenant T arrive AFTER t_destroy and are silently rejected (or worse, accepted under stale skew-bound assumption); PHASE B's healthy-only contract is silently violated.
stressors.solution: audit_destruct_sequencer's PHASE B precondition MUST re-validate hlc_service-status=healthy AT COMMIT TIME (CAS precondition includes hlc_service current mode + per-region mode envelope at f_T window) AND every drain-ack contributing to observed_ack_hlc must carry its emit-region's continuous-healthy-mode attestation from f_T forward. If any contributing region degraded between drain-ack emit and PHASE B CAS commit, the proposal MUST be CAS-rejected (reason 'health-mode-regressed-mid-window') and t_destroy recomputed via the worst-case path with a fresh healthy-mode drain-ack required from the regressed region. hlc_service handle MUST publish per-region mode-transition events with HLC stamps to lane_control so the sequencer can detect regressions deterministically.

stressors.description: credential_validator is collecting M-of-N signatures for a high-value override (e.g., PREPARED-ORPHAN recovery, or decommission-handoff-loss-attestation). At signature N-1 of M, credential_roster broadcasts compromise-revocation for one of the already-collected signers with retroactive-as-of-HLC strictly before the override's signing-window-start. The validator is ALREADY past the fast-reject phase (signers were valid at collection time); the partial collection now contains an invalid signature but the validator's commit-time CAS check uses the named roster_version's current state — does retroactive revocation invalidate it?
stressors.attractor: Either: (a) the override admits with a retroactively-revoked signer (audit-bypass attack vector) because the validator only checks compromise-revoked at collection time; or (b) the validator silently drops M-of-N short of M and stalls, with no operator visibility, and a high-value override (e.g., PREPARED-ORPHAN recovery for tenant_key blocking erasure attestation) hangs.
stressors.solution: credential_validator's commit-time CAS precondition MUST include the FULL retroactive-as-of-HLC list for every signer in the partial collection at commit-time (not just compromise-revoked-at-collection-time); if ANY signer's compromise-revoked-as-of-HLC is <= the signature's collection-HLC, the override is CAS-rejected with reason 'signer-retroactively-revoked' AND credential_validator emits an explicit override-stalled event onto lane_control + paged on-call carrying override_id, missing-signer-count, retroactive-revoke-cause; the override may be re-attempted with a fresh signer pool. credential_validator MUST treat partial-collection abandonment as a typed audit event (compliance_audit_owner) with full attribution; never silent.

stressors.description: Writer A drains, cannot flush within teardown window, writes a drain-ack-handoff record naming successor B. B accepts the handoff. Concurrently, B is itself scheduled for decommission. teardown_interlock's decommission rule says B's pending-flush handoff records must be resolved or transferred-to-another-successor C. C accepts; meanwhile, two more writers D and E also drain and hand off to C in the same window. teardown_interlock now must orchestrate recursive transfers; if the recursion graph has any cycle (A→B→C→A) or if a transfer-target is itself unhealthy mid-transfer, the SLA contract may be silently lost — and ack-by-handoff was supposed to be terminal.
stressors.attractor: Handoff records orphan onto a decommissioned buffer; PHASE B audit-key destruction stalls forever waiting for resolution; OR the recursive transfer admits a cycle, no buffer is owner of record, and the handoff drops silently with no compliance_audit entry. Either way, certificate-of-deletion is unprovable.
stressors.solution: teardown_interlock MUST maintain an explicit handoff-ownership-graph in lane_control; every transfer-of-handoff CAS proposal includes a no-cycle-precondition (target is not already an ancestor of source in the current ownership graph) and target-healthy-precondition (target is not itself in admitted decommission state). Cycle-rejection reason 'handoff-cycle-detected'; unhealthy-target rejection reason 'transfer-target-decommissioning'. If no other healthy transfer-target exists, teardown_interlock raises a handoff-orphan-imminent event onto lane_control + paged on-call AND blocks the source's decommission until either a fresh transfer-target appears OR an operator-elevated M-of-N (validated through credential_validator) approves resolved-with-loss-attestation. audit_destruct_sequencer MUST treat resolved-with-loss-attestation as PHASE B precondition only after this attestation lands.

stressors.description: bulk_admitter's wave-admission CAS proposal precondition reads (a) lease_issuer's lease-revoke sub-budget headroom AND (b) per-writer bounded queue depth from lane_control. Both metrics are published with HLC stamps. Under hlc_service skew-degraded mode, the published timestamps of these metrics may be substantially behind real-time; quorum_core CAS commit re-validates the precondition snapshot atomically — but the snapshot may itself be aged by tens of seconds. Wave admits over-throughput because the queue-depth metric was stale; named writers receive more drain-fence broadcasts than they can ack within window; ack windows expire; offboarding_orchestrator phase markers regress; PHASE B audit-key destruction stalls for a flood of tenants simultaneously.
stressors.attractor: Under HLC-degraded mode, bulk_admitter's exponential-with-jitter backoff is computed against stale precondition snapshots and converges to over-admission; cascade: ack window expirations → mass phase marker regression → PHASE B stall on tens of thousands of tenants → audit-key destruction backlog → compliance attestation deadline breach.
stressors.solution: bulk_admitter's wave-admission CAS proposal precondition MUST attach an explicit max-precondition-age field; quorum_core CAS commit re-validates the snapshot age against current hlc_service mode-aware bound; if the snapshot is older than max-precondition-age * (1 + hlc_skew_factor) under current mode, the proposal is CAS-rejected with reason 'precondition-snapshot-stale-under-degraded-hlc'. Under hlc_service skew-degraded mode, bulk_admitter MUST shrink max-tenants-per-wave by a documented factor and lengthen inter-wave spacing; the degraded-mode wave envelope is published as a typed envelope on lane_control. lease_issuer and named-writer queue-depth publishers MUST tag their published metrics with hlc_service-status at emit time so bulk_admitter can refuse to admit on precondition snapshots tagged with degraded mode unless the proposal explicitly opts in (operator override).

stressors.description: credential_roster issues compromise-revocation with retroactive-as-of-HLC f_rev. broadcast_pipeline begins re-emission. For tenant T1, offboarding_orchestrator's phase marker shows TERMINAL (ack-completed) under V_old — re-emission must be signature-only-update without window reset (per ir-resign-no-window-reset). For tenant T2, the marker shows ACK-EMITTED but the drain-ack itself was signed with a credential that is in the retroactive-revoke set. Is the prior ack still valid? The current rule treats ack-completed marker as terminal — but a retroactively-revoked drain-ack signature undermines the ack's validity. If broadcast_pipeline silently signature-only-updates without re-issuing a window for T2, an audit-bypass exists; if it always resets the window for retroactively-revoked-signer acks, mass churn.
stressors.attractor: Either silent audit-bypass: TERMINAL phase marker accepted despite drain-ack being retroactively-invalid; OR mass window churn for tenants whose drain-acks happen to be signed by a now-revoked but valid-at-ack-time credential, causing PHASE B stalls for thousands of tenants and back-pressure cascades.
stressors.solution: broadcast_pipeline's per-tenant signature-only-update path MUST consult drain-ack signing credentials per phase marker: for phase markers where the drain-ack itself was signed by a credential in the retroactive-revoke set under f_rev, the signature-only-update is INSUFFICIENT — broadcast_pipeline MUST escalate to a 'drain-ack-resign-required' state, retain the original phase marker (no window reset, no regression), and emit an explicit drain-ack-resign-request to the named writer through lane_control. Named writer responds by re-signing its existing drain-ack under the current roster_version (writer holds enough state); offboarding_orchestrator updates the phase marker's drain-ack signing version atomically. PHASE B's precondition for tenant T includes a 'no-retroactively-revoked-drain-ack-signers' check; audit_destruct_sequencer treats the drain-ack-resign-required state as PHASE-B-blocking only for affected tenants, not the entire wave.

stressors.description: Major incident: ops issues many simultaneous operator overrides — bulk-offboarding admissions, residency-2PC abort directives, PHASE-B loss-attestations, and probationary-fork admissions — all drawn from the same small operator-credential pool. credential_validator must collect M-of-N for each. Each operator's signing key is being requested across many concurrent overrides; signing throughput on the operator side becomes the bottleneck, while credential_validator's CAS-precondition checks pile up on lane_control.
stressors.attractor: credential_validator processes overrides in arrival-order; high-priority overrides (PREPARED-ORPHAN recovery blocking erasure) starve behind lower-priority overrides (probationary-fork admissions); operator pool is rate-limited so partial collections age out across overrides; the entire override channel under-throughputs in the moment when operators most need it.
stressors.solution: credential_validator MUST classify overrides into priority tiers (Tier-A: PREPARED-ORPHAN recovery, drain-ack loss-attestation; Tier-B: residency-2PC abort, decommission-handoff-loss; Tier-C: bulk-offboarding admission, probationary-fork) with a documented per-tier credential_validator throughput budget on lane_control. Higher-tier overrides admitted first; lower-tier overrides may be CAS-rejected with reason 'override-tier-deferred-by-higher-tier-incident' and a documented retry policy. Operator pool throughput is published into lane_control by credential_roster as a separate signal; credential_validator surfaces an override-channel-saturation back-pressure signal (lane_control + paged on-call) carrying per-tier pending counts and elapsed-collection-lag. Tier classification is itself recorded as a typed audit entry.

stressors.description: broadcast_pipeline's shed-and-defer is firing because residency 2PC PREPARE watermark is exceeded; PHASE A audit-key destruction broadcasts for a cohort of tenants are deferred via deferral records on lane_control. Concurrently, credential_roster issues compromise-revocation with retroactive-as-of-HLC overlapping the original-emission HLC of those NOT-YET-EMITTED-but-deferred entries. Are the deferred entries treated as in-flight broadcasts requiring re-sign? If yes, when they later re-emit at watermark-clear, what's their effective signing roster_version — original (now retroactively revoked) or current?
stressors.attractor: Either: (a) deferred entries re-emit under stale signing version and are immediately rejected by named writers (live-lock); (b) deferred entries are silently re-signed under current version losing the original sign-time anchoring (audit-trail gap); (c) the deferral records become orphans because re-emission logic doesn't iterate deferred entries on compromise-revocation.
stressors.solution: broadcast_pipeline's compromise-revocation handler MUST iterate deferred entries (queryable via the deferral records on lane_control) and apply the same drain-ack-resign-required / signature-only-update rules per entry's effective signing-state — a deferred entry that has never been emitted simply binds to current signing roster_version at re-emission time (no need to re-sign), but the deferral record's signing-version-at-defer field MUST be updated to reflect the current roster_version so audit trails remain coherent. The deferral record is itself a signed artifact and inherits the per-tenant signature-only-update rules. broadcast_pipeline emits an explicit 'deferred-entries-rebound-to-version-V' typed audit entry per cohort.

stressors.description: bulk_admitter publishes bulk-wave-end marker on lane_control as soon as the wave's broadcast_pipeline emit-cohort completes; but ack-completed phase markers and PHASE B audit-key DESTROYED entries for tenants in the wave continue to land on lane_control / lane_lease for hours afterward. health_lane consumers correlating classification entries via wave_id receive late entries that arrive AFTER wave-end; correlation drops; degradation-envelope expectation no longer matches observation.
stressors.attractor: bulk-wave correlation degrades — late drain-ack and PHASE B entries appear orphan to health_lane classifiers; on-call dashboards show wave 'completed' while audit-key destructions are still firing; alerting on degradation-envelope-deviation produces false positives because the envelope was scoped to the wave-emit window only.
stressors.solution: bulk_admitter MUST emit two distinct markers: bulk-wave-emit-end (when broadcast_pipeline finishes emitting the wave's drain-fence broadcasts) and bulk-wave-finalized (when audit_destruct_sequencer signals every tenant in the wave has either reached PHASE B DESTROYED or resolved-with-loss-attestation, OR the wave's documented finalization deadline has elapsed and any unfinalized tenants are surfaced as a wave-finalization-overflow event). wave_id correlation key references the marker class; degradation-envelope expectation MUST carry the marker-class tag so health_lane classifiers compare against the right window.

stressors.description: residency_lock for tenant T is acquired (PREPARE in flight) on writer A's region. Writer A is admitted for decommission via teardown_interlock. The 2PC PREPARE has not yet reached terminal; the HLC-bounded prepared-window for the lock is approaching expiry. teardown_interlock has rules for in-flight drain-fences but residency_lock is a separate state — does teardown_interlock check for in-flight residency-2PC PREPAREs against tenants whose lifecycle is bound to the decommissioning region? If not, the lock can be 'orphaned' on a torn-down region and PREPARED-ORPHAN may not be detected in time.
stressors.attractor: residency_lock state is left dangling on a decommissioned region's CAS namespace; PREPARED-ORPHAN detection delayed past the prepared-window; subsequent (tenant_key, V+2) PREPARE proposals are CAS-rejected without operator visibility; tenant T cannot make policy progress.
stressors.solution: teardown_interlock's node-decommission admission MUST include an 'in-flight-residency-2PC-PREPARE-set on this node' precondition (read from residency_lock state in lane_control); decommission is rejected with reason 'residency-2pc-in-flight-on-node' if any PREPARE is still active. residency_lock MUST publish a per-region in-flight-PREPARE-set onto lane_control. If decommission must proceed (operator-elevated), the abort-and-handoff path MUST atomically abort all in-flight PREPAREs on the decommissioning region (transitioning each to PREPARED-ORPHAN with audit) AND signal credential_validator to admit any pending (tenant_key, V+next) recovery PREPAREs on a successor region under elevated M-of-N.

stressors.description: Every subsystem (broadcast_pipeline, bulk_admitter, residency_lock, audit_destruct_sequencer, credential_validator, teardown_interlock) emits typed audit entries via ext_compliance_audit_owner. Under a major incident (override flood + bulk wave + compromise-revocation cascade), the audit channel itself saturates. compliance_audit_owner's ack-window for typed entries expires; subsystems must decide: stall the operational decision waiting for audit ack, or proceed and back-fill audit?
stressors.attractor: Either: (a) operational stall — every CAS proposal blocks waiting for compliance_audit_owner ack, livelocking the entire lifecycle_gate during the moment ops most needs it; (b) silent audit gap — subsystems proceed and back-fill, but a region failure between operational commit and audit back-fill loses the audit entry permanently.
stressors.solution: Subsystems MUST distinguish two audit modes: (a) inline-audit — for low-volume, high-integrity entries (override admissions, decommission-handoff-loss attestations, PHASE B DESTROYED), the operational CAS proposal is co-committed with the audit entry into ext_compliance_audit_owner via a single CAS proposal (atomic); rejection on audit failure rolls back operational decision. (b) deferred-audit — for high-volume entries (drain-fence broadcasts, deferral records, wave markers, back-pressure signals), the operational CAS commits independently and an audit-pending durable record is written to lane_control with the operational entry reference; a background flush pumps these into compliance_audit_owner; on saturation, lane_control retains the audit-pending records (durably) and an audit-back-pressure event is paged. Subsystems publish their audit-pending count onto lane_control so compliance_audit_owner can prioritize drain. Tier-A operational decisions (PHASE B, override) are inline; everything else is deferred. The classification per audit-entry-type is documented.

stressors.description: lifecycle_gate quorum lost a region during a partition. On region recovery, the recovering replica must re-derive in-flight state from lane_control: in-flight residency_lock entries, deferral records, partial-collection overrides, pending wave markers, drain-ack-handoff records. credential_validator's partial-signature collections are not on lane_control until commit — they live in process memory. On re-entry, the recovering replica has no view of in-flight collections; the operator pool may have already signed but the validator has lost the partial state.
stressors.attractor: Partial M-of-N collections silently dropped on recovery; operators see signed overrides that never admit; bulk-wave admissions and PHASE-B operations stall waiting on overrides whose validators never resume; recovery requires manual operator intervention to re-issue every override mid-incident.
stressors.solution: credential_validator MUST persist partial-signature collections as durable collection-checkpoint records on lane_control (signed by the replica, with collection_id + per-signer signature + collection_HLC + override-class). On re-entry, the recovering replica re-reads collection-checkpoints and resumes collection from the last checkpoint. Partial collections older than a configurable grace window without progress are typed-audited as 'collection-abandoned-on-recovery' and operator is paged. credential_validator's collection-checkpoint write IS itself a deferred-audit entry per r-audit-mode-classification.
